status: sixth aggregation slice: destinations retain their ordered fold state and resume from the unchanged prefix, cutting NovyWave diagnostics 14.9% with byte-identical diagnostics and plans

change.what: every requirement destination now retains the resolved contributor list of its last fold and the aggregate after every prefix of that list. The next fold compares the ordered lists, restores the stored prefix aggregate at the last common term, and merges only the remaining suffix; the new prefix list is retained in turn. This replaces the homogeneous single-pass fold, which could not expose prefix aggregates.
change.why_this_is_the_mandate: the contract asks that a committed site change update a destination without re-merging unchanged contributors. The probe measured 94,908 reusable prefix terms against 119,920 NovyWave contributor visits (79%) and 31,281 of 35,616 on TodoMVC (88%).
change.soundness: merging in this path never binds a variable (every call is permanent=false) and structural widening is a cached pure function, so the aggregate after any prefix is a function of that prefix alone. Restoring a stored prefix aggregate is therefore exactly the value the full fold would compute, and the suffix merges continue with the same left-fold operation in the same order. Withdrawal, replacement and alias reordering shrink the common prefix and recompute the affected suffix, so the old semantics are reproduced rather than approximated.
change.state: one map entry per refreshed destination holding two boxed slices (contributor terms and prefix aggregates); a collapsed prefix costs one slice copy.

phase_probe_release.note: pairs are [pre-slice build, retained-prefix build]; one release observation per fixture and build
